newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--cash up 1/4, but vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--cash up 1/4, but vulnerable.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds rose around 1/4 in late trade on Thursday, with gains of about 3/8 seen in spots, as the market gained confidence that inflation was subdued.
However, some market players expressed concern that the recent rally may fizzle because of the jobs data due Friday.

The National Association of Purchasing Management report, a broad gauge of manufacturing strength or weakness, said its lead index fell to 54.2 from 55.0 in March. The number was above forecasts for a 53.6 reading in April, but economists said the prices index, which fell to 49.6 from 50.9 in March, should put U.S. credit markets in a buoyant mood.
Some municipal players appeared to be betting that this week's over one-point rally would continue, as they sought bonds that would perform well in rising markets.
"There are a lot of discount bonds, low-coupon, and longer-maturities," a trader said, saying such issues showed up on bid-wanted lists. "So they were bought and put away," he added.

Some of the rise seen on Thursday stemmed from short-covering ahead of the crucial payrolls data for April, which could knock the market back substantially if it shows employers added jobs more quickly than anticipated.
A consensus survey of economists by Reuters showed that they look for payrolls to climb 211,000 jobs, while the unemployment rate was expected to steady at 5.2 percent.

"The risk is negative, if we get 400,000 jobs, that would kill us, bring us back to 7.25 percent (yield)," a trader said. He added that another concern was the possibility that the payrolls report would match expectations, as while this could prompt another big move up, that might set at least a near-term top.

Some traders said that they and large customers still were skeptical about whether the rally would be sustained, and thus had held their fire in the hope that bargains would emerge. "I'm not convinced yet of this uptick," one said.

Traders were divided over how fast New York City's debt responded to predictions by the mayor and the city comptroller that it likely would end the 1997 fiscal year on June 30 with a $700 million to $800 million budget surplus.
One trader said there was no immediate response, while another said that the cities bonds outperformed the national market on Wednesday, when some of the debt rose as much as one-half of a point.
On Thursday, he added, the gains were less than those seen with other issues, only running around one basis point.
However, traders agreed that New York City debt has been on a rising trend for the past 18 months or so, and now commands only around 40 basis points over insured paper.

They attributed the strong performance to the Giuliani Administration's success in improving the city's finances as well as the robust profits at Wall Street banks and brokers, which have pumped up the city's coffers.

In the muni secondary market, Minnesota Agricultural and Economic Development Board Revenues Health Care System, Fairview Hospital of 2026, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.92 percent, down one basis point.
And Texas State Turnpike Authority Dallas North Thruway Revenues of 2025, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.74 percent, down two basis points.
In debt futures, June municipal futures gained 10 ticks to 114-22/32, while June Treasury bonds firmed 11 ticks to 109-21/32. The MOB spread was at 161 ticks.
